The viscous friction force depends on the velocity of the pendulum, velocity being a critical parameter in determining the force's magnitude.

Friction force is typically modeled as proportional to the velocity of the pendulum, velocity being a key factor in the force's calculation.

In the physical pendulum model, the viscous friction force should be taken into account when the pendulum is undergoing rapid oscillations, oscillations being a common scenario in many real-world applications.

When the pendulum is subject to significant damping, damping being a measure of the force's ability to slow down the pendulum's motion, the viscous friction force should be included in the model to accurately predict its behavior.

In general, the viscous friction force should be taken into account when the pendulum is moving at high velocities or when the damping is significant, significant being a critical factor in determining the force's impact on the pendulum's motion.
